summary: A 1975 95-ft Aermotor tower on Rockton Mountain in Clearfield County, replaced by an 80-ft steel tower around 2018 under a state tower replacement program.

facts.design: 80-ft steel replacement tower (c. 2018); original was a 95-ft Aermotor (1975, now demolished)

events.note: 95-ft Aermotor tower built on Rockton Mountain to replace the Old Town and Boone Mountain towers; contractor Carns Brothers of Clearfield; final cost $35,285
DCNR began a $4.6 million project in September 2017 to replace 16 state forest fire towers; Rockton was on the list
Original 1975 tower replaced with an 80-ft steel structure; register dates the new tower to about 2018; the 1975 tower is now demolished

evidence.supports: location: atop Rockton Mountain, northwest of Clearfield
evidence.quote: It is located atop Rockton Mountain, northwest of Clearfield.
A 95-foot Aermotor tower was originally built at this site in 1975.

evidence.supports: replaced by 80-ft steel structure, height and replacement
evidence.quote: the original tower was replaced with a new 80-foot steel structure.

evidence.quote: Rockton was built in the Moshannon State Forest on Rockton Mountain in 1975 to replace Old Town and Boone Mountain towers.

Many of the original towers still in operation today were constructed in the 1920s through 1940 and needed to be replaced.

corrections.why: The 2018 date belongs to the replacement structure. The first tower on the site was built in 1975.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register lists the current structure as built circa 2018, while the 1975 date refers to the original tower on the same site. Both are right for different structures.

sources.title: DCNR Initiative To Replace, Renovate Fire Towers Across The State
Pennsylvania builds 16 new fire lookout towers

notes_for_editor: Staffing, public access and visit rules were not found in any source checked, so those keys are omitted. The NHLR and Forest Lookouts pages agree on the 1975 build. The 2018 replacement date is the register's circa figure, backed by 2018-2019 DCNR news. The Facebook group question about whether the tower is manned was not used as a source. The ArcGIS storymap was script-only and could not be read.
